newsitem.title: USA: Figure in fund-raising scandal to testify-report.
newsitem.headline: Figure in fund-raising scandal to testify-report.

text.p: A central figure in the Democratic fund-raising scandal said he would testify at congressional hearings if he was subpoenaed, the Daily News reported Monday.

John Huang, a former top fund-raiser for President Clinton, denied he funnelled money from foreign governments into Clinton's re-election campaign. "I don't know if foreign governments have (given money)," he said. "If there is money, I haven't seen it."
He said he would testify at congressional hearings scheduled to begin early in July if he was subpoenaed. He declined to discuss details of the numerous allegations against him.

Last week Gerald Solomon, a New York Republican, said intelligence showed Huang had passed classified government data to his former employer, the Lippo Group of Indonesia. Investigators are also examining Huang's role in alleged attempts by the Chinese government to pump $2 million into U.S. political campaigns.

Huang spoke to the Daily News Sunday after delivering the keynote speech at an annual banquet of graduates from a military academy in Taiwan. He told the all-Chinese audience that immigrants should take an active part in politics and explained his enthusiasm for Democratic fund-raising.
"If you are a doctor you can only cure one person at a time. But if you enter the policy-making level, you can affect 10,000 people."
